lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: A road win can lift a team; this one also exposed the cost of doing business. The Maple Leafs' 6-3 victory over Colorado was powered by William Nylander's two goals and three assists, but Chris Tanev's first-period upper-body injury cast a long shadow over the celebration. Tanev managed only five shifts before leaving, and Toronto now waits for clarity on the veteran defender who remains the back-end's anchor. Auston Matthews chipped in four points, while the Leafs' attack finally looked as dangerous as its reputation. At 3-2-1, Toronto sits fourth in the Atlantic with seven points, one behind the division lead - a respectable start, but hardly a cushion. The win stopped the wobble after the 4-3 loss to Vegas and made the warning plain: this club can score its way out of trouble, but it cannot casually lose Tanev. Next comes Tuesday's 9 p.m. visit to Utah's Mammoth, where the first question is who replaces his minutes.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and Toronto's work begins with an uncomfortable truth: a 79-83 finish in fifth place in the AL East demands more than cosmetic repairs. The immediate story is the organization's Arizona Fall League audition, where Blue Jays prospects - including JoJo Parker and a raw-tools standout such as Jake Cook - are being asked to make the future impossible to ignore. That matters because the major-league core needs help now, not another winter of wishful thinking. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is the central problem and the central hope; veteran advice from Joey Votto - "watch your dad" - lands as both wisdom and indictment. Toronto must build protection around its star, reinforce the bullpen and settle the infield's Ernie Clement question before camp. Watch the Fall League closely: the next credible answer may already be wearing a Blue Jays uniform in Arizona.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors left Vancouver with more than an exhibition win - they left with a lineup question demanding an answer. Toronto beat the Clippers 114-106 on Saturday, a result that does not count in the standings but offered a useful glimpse of the team's emerging interior pairing. Collin Murray-Boyles attacked the lane, finished with 13 points and nine rebounds, and shared stretches with Jakob Poeltl - precisely the experiment coach Darko Rajaković called "super important." RJ Barrett led Toronto with 20 points, while Immanuel Quickley added 18, giving the projected core some needed rhythm. The bittersweet subplot was Gradey Dick's return in a Clippers uniform; Toronto's former first-round pick scored four points in 13 minutes. The Raptors are 1-1 in preseason, with cuts and rotation decisions still ahead. Tuesday's meeting with the Knicks is the next test of Murray-Boyles beside Poeltl - and of who survives the final roster squeeze before the Oct. 21 opener against Chicago.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The slogans are intact; the season is not. Washington's latest collapse, a 30-13 loss to Indianapolis, dropped the Commanders to 1-3 and fourth in the NFC East, with a one-game losing streak and two games separating them from the top. The immediate story is Jayden Daniels' return to the starting lineup against the Giants after missing two games with an elbow dislocation - a needed jolt for an offense that has lost its rhythm. Sam Cosmi and Rachaad White are also expected back, but the injury list remains crowded: Stefon Diggs is out, while Terry McLaurin remains a game-time decision with a hamstring injury. The Cowboys' stumble has opened a narrow door, but Washington must stop admiring it. Sunday's 1 p.m. meeting with New York is the test: Daniels must make the opportunity count before the season's drift becomes a verdict.

article.title: Nylander Leads Leafs Past Avalanche
paragraphs: William Nylander scored twice and added three assists as the Leafs beat the Avalanche 6-3 in Denver, tying his career high with five points and reaching 700 NHL points. Easton Cowan also scored, while Chris Tanev left with an upper-body injury. Toronto is 3-2-1 and visits the Mammoth Tuesday at 9:00 p.m. ET on TSN.

The Blue Jays are turning toward the Arizona Fall League, where prospects will get a fresh stage, while Toronto evaluates JoJo Parker and other young players. The Raptors beat the Clippers 114-106 in a preseason game, with RJ Barrett scoring 20 points and Scottie Barnes grabbing 10 rebounds. Toronto faces the Knicks Tuesday before opening the regular season against Chicago on October 21.

The Commanders host the Giants at 1:00 p.m. ET on Fox. Terry McLaurin is questionable with a hamstring injury, while Owens and Omenihu are out. Washington enters at 1-3, with McLaurin's status expected near kickoff.
